problem: BeBee had no production input binding and no runtime proof that input reaches a collection-proxy world, that modal UI can consume it before gameplay and lower main-world listeners, or that focus returns correctly after the modal closes.

decision.rationale: Use Defold's documented input stacks directly: a lower main-world sentinel acquires focus first, the main-world collection-proxy owner acquires above it, proxied gameplay acquires focus in its own world, and a modal listener acquires later focus and returns true while open. Exact-head Chromium events prove propagation into the proxy world, cross-stack consumption, and restoration. T-010 remains a hypothesis because this ticket does not prove the proxy memory/lifecycle budget.

research.candidate_pool_exception: Comparable shipped-product research is not applicable to an engine input-routing proof; the observable behavior is defined by Defold runtime contracts.
research.reference_exception: No player-facing touch layout or movement feel is selected in BB-003.

anti_pattern.observation: A proxy-loaded world does not receive input merely because its listeners acquire focus; the proxy owner must also participate in the main input stack.
anti_pattern.lesson: Do not replace the missing owner-focus proof with assumptions or a custom forwarding layer.

official_docs.verified_constraint: Objects in a collection loaded through a collection proxy receive input only when the game object containing the proxy participates in input focus routing.
Each proxy-loaded world has its own input stack; listeners there are processed before dispatch continues down the main stack, and returning true consumes the action across that nested traversal.
Single-touch input is available through the mouse-button-one binding path, allowing one semantic pointer action for mouse and single touch in this P0 proof.
Chromium CDP can dispatch deterministic keyboard and touch events into the actual HTML5 build used by CI; the probe holds states across animation frames so Defold samples pressed/released edges.

alternatives.reason: Matches Defold's native lifecycle and input semantics and can be tested end-to-end in the HTML5 target without inventing a second routing system.
Forwarding raw input as custom messages would duplicate engine focus semantics and could conceal the exact proxy propagation risk BB-003 exists to prove.
Deferring the proof would allow region/screen architecture to scale on an untested assumption explicitly called out by T-010 and T-011.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Movement and primary actions are represented by semantic action IDs with keyboard aliases rather than gameplay consuming raw keys.
acceptance_criteria.evidence: app/game.input_binding maps W/Up, S/Down, A/Left, D/Right and Space/Enter into shared semantic actions consumed through app/input_semantics.lua.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: HTML5 mouse and single touch share an explicit pointer abstraction without prematurely selecting final touch movement UX.
acceptance_criteria.evidence: MOUSE_BUTTON_1 maps to pointer_primary; Defold's documented single-touch mapping and exact-head Chromium touch dispatch exercise that semantic path.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Input propagates from the main-world proxy owner into the loaded gameplay world and then continues to a lower main-world listener when unconsumed.
acceptance_criteria.evidence: The exact-head runtime smoke establishes sentinel focus below proxy-owner focus and requires one W event to produce both proxied gameplay and lower-main-stack sentinel move_up markers.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: An open modal consumes relevant input before gameplay and lower listeners on the main-world stack, then releasing it restores normal delivery.
acceptance_criteria.evidence: The exact-head runtime smoke opens the modal with Esc, requires modal-only W delivery, forbids gameplay/sentinel leakage, closes the modal, then requires gameplay/sentinel W delivery again.

automated: Defold runtime evidence builds development and release HTML5 bundles from the exact PR head.

tools/defold/chromium_input_proxy_smoke.py dispatches actual Chromium key/touch events, holds their state across animation frames, and writes runtime-evidence/input-proxy-smoke.json; any missing/forbidden marker fails the job.
Repository standards and trusted-base PR evidence gates run independently on the candidate diff.
verification.runtime_errors: The exact-head browser smoke fails if CDP reports runtime exceptions or if expected focus/input markers are missing.

known_limitations: BB-003 proves input ownership/propagation and modal consumption, not collection-proxy memory cost or the complete region/screen lifecycle policy; T-010 therefore remains HYPOTHESIS.
The final touch movement control and its geometry remain a P1 player-facing decision; BB-003 only proves the shared pointer/touch abstraction.
